[omnibox] Support CrossDeviceTabProvider zero-suggest matches on Android

Previously, GROUP_CROSS_DEVICE_TABS was only included in the Desktop and
iOS ZPS grouper sections. On Android, CrossDeviceTabProvider::Start()
created CROSS_DEVICE_TAB matches, but AutocompleteResult::SortAndCull()
silently dropped them because GROUP_CROSS_DEVICE_TABS was missing from
AndroidNTPZpsSection, AndroidSRPZpsSection, and AndroidWebZpsSection.

This patch:
- Adds GROUP_CROSS_DEVICE_TABS (limit 1) to AndroidNTPZpsSection,
  AndroidSRPZpsSection, and AndroidWebZpsSection (updating the group
  index in AndroidNTPZpsSection::InitFromMatches).
- Defines kCrossDeviceTabZeroSuggestRelevance (1450) in
  suggestion_group_util.h so cross-device tab matches sort below
  contextual actions (1500) and above remote zero-prefix suggestions
  (550-1400), satisfying the ZpsSection::InitFromMatches ordering
  invariant.
- Skips CROSS_DEVICE_TAB suggestions alongside CLIPBOARD_* in Android's
  AutocompleteResult.serialize() so ephemeral cross-device tab matches
  are not persisted to SharedPreferences ZPS cache across cold starts.

[CodeHealth] Migrate AudioDataS16Converter to interleaved_data_cast

Migrate `AudioDataS16Converter::ConvertToAudioDataS16()` and
`AudioDataS16ConverterTest` away from the deprecated
`AudioBuffer::channels()` method and `reinterpret_span` casts.

Use `AudioBuffer::interleaved_data_cast<int16_t>()` instead, which
provides runtime verification that the buffer is interleaved and
format-compatible.

media: Use WeakPtr in MojoCodecFactory to prevent dangling pointers

MojoCodecFactory and its derived classes (MojoCodecFactoryMojoDecoder
and MojoCodecFactoryFuchsia) post a task to media_task_runner_ during
construction with base::Unretained(this) to bind Mojo remotes. If the
instance is destroyed before the task executes, the task runner invokes
BindOnTaskRunner with a dangling pointer, triggering a crash in
PartitionAlloc's dangling raw_ptr detector.

This CL fixes the crash by using base::WeakPtrFactory to pass WeakPtrs
to the posted tasks and disconnect/response handlers instead of
base::Unretained.

Revert "[omnibox] Drop bottom shadow margin on collapsed Full WebUI popup"

This reverts commit 6ec72c2362ffa58e57ce401023fba33f32fd1c8f.

Reason for revert: interactive_ui_tests crashed in
FullWebUIOmniboxInteractiveTest tests because IN_PROC_BROWSER_TEST_F
was used instead of IN_PROC_BROWSER_TEST_P with parameterized fixture

Failure Link: https://ci.chromium.org/b/8669280240164072353

Original change's description:
> [omnibox] Drop bottom shadow margin on collapsed Full WebUI popup
>
> While collapsed (no suggestions visible), the Full WebUI popup widget
> still reserves a 28px bottom shadow margin[1][2]. This creates an
> invisible strip below the Omnibox that covers the web contents, causing
> clicks just below the popup to be swallowed or fail to dismiss the
> Omnibox on the first click.
>
> This CL:
>
> 1. Drops the bottom shadow margin to 0 when collapsed, sizing the popup
>    flush to the bottom of the location bar pill so clicks beneath it
>    reach the page immediately.
> 2. Restores the full 28px bottom margin when the dropdown expands so the
>    drop shadow renders completely.
> 3. Insets the outside-click hit-test in `OnEvent()` by the shadow
>    margin.
> 4. Prevents default in `full_app.ts` on non-focusable mousedown targets
>    so clicks on the focus ring or padding don't accidentally blur the
>    input.
>

dbus: Let desktop Linux end the session instead of crashing when a bus is lost

Since https://crrev.com/307419 (https://crbug.com/432980) Bus aborts
with LOG(FATAL) when libdbus delivers the local Disconnected signal.
That fits Chrome OS, where a dbus-daemon crash takes the device down
anyway, but on desktop Linux the session and system buses routinely go
away under a running browser: at logout, on `systemctl --user restart
dbus`, or when dbus-broker is restarted by a package upgrade. Each of
those currently ends in a browser crash report rather than an exit.

Add Bus::Options::disconnected_callback, posted to the origin thread
when the connection is lost. When it is unset the behaviour is
unchanged (FATAL, same message), so Chrome OS and every existing
caller keep today's semantics.

Give the shared desktop buses that callback from the browser. They
were lazily created NoDestructor statics with no way to pass options,
and in unit tests a bus cached by one test held a freed per-test
ThreadPool runner in the next (ASan use-after-free, TSan "Check failed:
delegate"). dbus_thread_linux now has one heap-owned object that starts
a dedicated D-Bus thread and creates both buses up front:
Initialize(disconnected_callback) sets the callback, creating the object
if a getter has not already done so, and Shutdown() tears it down for
tests. The browser initializes it in
PreCreateMainMessageLoop(), before content's PowerMonitor takes the
system bus, with the closure it already runs when the display server
connection is lost (ChromeBrowserMainExtraPartsOzone): run
chrome::SessionEnding() and treat a failure to exit as fatal. The
browser does not call Shutdown() at exit because the in-process device
service is destroyed after the last BrowserMainParts hook and still
holds bus-owned ObjectProxy objects; the buses are released with the
process. Processes that never call Initialize() get the buses created
on first use, without a callback, as before.

The dbus_thread_linux rework builds on nerima@'s
https://crrev.com/c/8009126, reshaped per hashimoto@'s review there:
no lock, one owned instance, and an explicit Initialize() for the
callback. The getters still create the instance on first use for
embedders and test harnesses that never call Initialize(); the header
carries a TODO to make Initialize() mandatory once they all do.

Closing a private connection right after connecting it makes
ThreadSanitizer report a lock-order inversion between two mutexes
inside libdbus, the same third-party inversion already suppressed for
Bus::ShutdownAndBlock (crbug.com/455638); the new test is the first to
close one outside that path, so the suppression now covers libdbus by
module.

Bug: none
Test: dbus_unittests.BusTest.DisconnectedCallback

[NTP Customization Sync] Clear stale NTP background SharedPreferences on theme change

Previously, the NTP background SharedPreferences were cleaned up by
type-specific helpers (cleanupChromeColors(), resetCustomizedImage(),
cleanupOnBackgroundTypeChanged()). As a result, data of a previous
theme could leak across transitions, e.g. hex colors, the daily refresh
keys, the image file path, or the prefs of a pending synced theme when
the user resets before it is applied (such as Synced Set Up "Undo"),
while some keys were removed multiple times in a single transition.

This CL makes the SharedPreferences always describe exactly one theme:
the one to load on next startup. All the NTP background keys are
cleared once via
NtpCustomizationUtils.removeAllNtpBackgroundDataFromSharedPreference()
before a new background is persisted, at the following entry points:
- onBackgroundDataChanged().
- onSyncedThemeCollectionImageChanged(), onSyncedChromeColorChanged()
  and onSyncedDefaultThemeReset(). These still don't change the active
  in-memory state.
- onBackgroundInitializationFailed(), when the active background fails
  to initialize and no synced theme is pending.
- The policy reset.
The rest of the code only writes the SharedPreferences. The redundant
cleanup helpers are removed, and the remaining helpers are renamed to
deleteAllNtpBackgroundImageFiles() and
resetNtpCustomBackgroundDataForPolicy().

Image file deletion is separated from the SharedPreferences cleanup:
- cleanupBackgroundImage() resets the in-memory image state, and deletes
  the image files only when switching away from an image background
  with sync disabled. When sync is enabled, the files are shared with
  the theme history lists and are cleaned up by
  NtpBackgroundDataManager.
- onSyncedChromeColorChanged() and onSyncedDefaultThemeReset() no longer
  delete the image files directly; they are handled when the synced
  theme is applied. Synced themes are only received when theme sync is
  enabled.

Other changes:
- The initialization of the background image no longer writes the
  background type or removes the Chrome color keys, which could
  overwrite a pending synced theme. The background type is now
  persisted once in onBackgroundDataChanged() for all the types.
- The Chrome color daily refresh flag is persisted from the selected
  data.
- Upload images selected from the history list (without a bitmap) now
  persist their type, background info and primary color, so they are
  loaded on next startup.
- The policy reset also clears the COLOR_FROM_HEX data and the image
  file path.

[PA] Use `kNoOverrideHooks` explicitly for the internal partition

The internal partition allocates with a named constant,
kInternalAllocFlags = kNoHooks | kNoOverrideHooks, instead of kNoHooks
alone. It holds PartitionAlloc's own data (e.g. thread caches), so no
hook may observe or serve its allocations.

No change in behavior: today kNoHooks already skips the override
hooks. I plan to remove this implicit relation soon and this CL is the
first step.

[PA] Pack BucketSizeDetails into one word and pass it by value

BucketSizeDetails becomes a class that packs `bucket_index` and
`slot_size` into one 64-bit word. It is passed by value everywhere
instead of by const reference. No change in behavior.

This change allows us to save number of registers usage per function
call.

Revert "[Cast] Only show report cast issue menu item when feedback is allowed"

This reverts commit 271d03a434f48d85bff36c1383461ca8305a77dc.

Reason for revert: Causes deterministic test failure in
CastContextualMenuBrowserTest.EnableAndDisableReportIssue on
linux-chromeos-chrome. The test verifies that
kActionMediaToolbarContextReportCastIssue is absent from the
contextual menu when policy::key::kUserFeedbackAllowed is disabled.
However, on ChromeOS, updating the policy via
provider()->UpdateChromePolicy() does not dynamically rebuild or
update the browser action items created during browser initialization,
causing std::ranges::contains(disabled_actions,
kActionMediaToolbarContextReportCastIssue) to remain true.

Failure Link: https://ci.chromium.org/b/8669281911997113649

Original change's description:
> [Cast] Only show report cast issue menu item when feedback is allowed
>
> When user feedback is disallowed (e.g. by enterprise policy or account
> capabilities), CastFeedbackUIConfig disables the chrome://cast-feedback
> WebUI. Previously, the Cast toolbar button contextual menu added the
> "Report an issue with Google Cast" action unconditionally, resulting
> in an unrouted navigation ("This site can't be reached") when clicked.
>
> This CL gates the action creation in CastToolbarButtonUtil on
> chrome::CanShowFeedback(bwi->GetProfile()), matching the behavior of
> MediaToolbarButtonContextualMenu.
>
> Fixed: 554178186

Revert "Prevent Glic experimental triggering handler cleanup on self-superseded invocations."

This reverts commit 39ef7e499af513a02219c1d36d91ecccbf8e8443.

Reason for revert: Consistently failing GlicExperimentalTriggeringMessageHandlerBrowserTest.testDuplicateTriggerMessageReturnsErrorWithoutUaf on Linux Tests.

Failure Link:
- https://ci.chromium.org/ui/p/chromium/builders/ci/Linux%20Tests/186928/overview
- https://ci.chromium.org/ui/p/chromium/builders/ci/Win10%20Tests%20x64/112740/overview
- https://ci.chromium.org/ui/p/chromium/builders/ci/Mac13%20Tests/42997/overview

Diagnosis:
The addition of `if (!pending_invoke_ids_.empty()) return;` in `OnInvokeError` causes errors on secondary invocations (such as duplicate triggers returning synchronous `kInvokeInProgress`) to be ignored if the original invocation is still in flight. Because `OnInvokeError` returns early without calling `HandleTerminalUpdate`, the expected FAILED task update message is never emitted, causing `testDuplicateTriggerMessageReturnsErrorWithoutUaf` to time out waiting on `future.Take()`.

Original change's description:
> Prevent Glic experimental triggering handler cleanup on self-superseded invocations.
>
> Experimental triggering updates handlers are shared per context id, so a
> continuation request invokes on the same handler that owns the in-flight
> invocation it supersedes. GlicInvokeHandler::OnError() posts the
> kSuperseded error asynchronously, so the handler previously tore itself
> down (and stopped delivering updates) on the next task, even though the
> continuation invocation was still in flight and waiting for updates.
>
> Track the set of in-flight invocation IDs (`pending_invoke_ids_`) on
> ExperimentalTriggeringUpdatesHandler, removing each ID in
> OnInvokeSuccess() and OnInvokeError(), and ignore errors while another
> invocation started by the same handler remains in flight.
>
> Change-Id: Ica56ab66b844ebc693a87ac1e9b7d67acfcb2a81

Fix TabStripComboButton Not Rendering Bug

This fixes a bug where the tab search button is not rendering in the old
horizontal tab strip if we start the browser with the pref toggled off,
and we later toggle the pref on via context menu or settings.

This bug was happening because the FlexLayout manager of
HorizontalTabStripRegionViewOld was setting the visibility of the combo
button as false. Then when the combo button is visible, we set the its
kViewIgnoredByLayoutKey property as true, so the layout manager does not
change the visibility of the combo button view.

To fix this, we instead kViewIgnoredByLayoutKey in the constructor of
the parent view HorizontalTabStripRegionViewOld. This way the layout
manager does not change its visibility at all, and it remains its
default value (true).

[Vertical Tabs] Keep collapsed positioning for expand-on-hover rail.

When the rail expands on hover, keep its internal layout `positions` the
same as in the collapsed state, so the rail extends rather than re-lays
out, while internal row `content` still show expanded content:

- shouldUseCollapsedPositioning(): rail-level, true for COLLAPSED and
  hover. Decides where things sit (margins, height, header buttons,
  separator).
- shouldShowIconOnly(): internal-content-level, true when collapsed,
  or for pinned rows outside hover. Decides what a row shows (title,
  icons, end padding).

Besides, vertical_tab_group_header now get their start inset from the
title margin, like vertical_tab_item get theirs from the favicon margin.
Both layout now rely on the child view's start margin instead of the
root view's start padding.

Demo: http://screencast/cast/NDkyODMzODExOTM2MDUxMnw1MDRkNjEzMi0yMw

[wtf] Make Vector::UncheckedIterator advance checks DCHECK-only

In release builds with Vector modification checks enabled, checking for
modifications on both iterator dereference (operator*, operator->,
operator[]) and iterator advancement (operator++, operator--,
operator+=, operator-=) emits two modification checks per loop
iteration. If the loop body may write to memory that aliases uint32_t,
the compiler must reload modification_state_.count from the Vector on
both *it and ++it.

Restrict the checks in iterator advance operators to DCHECK builds
(DCheckModifications()), while keeping CheckModifications() in all
dereference operators so any element access after a Vector mutation is
still caught in release builds.

CONV=faa0d6f3-6c3b-4254-a2f2-3f8e82f4004a

[wtf] Parameterize Vector::UncheckedIterator on kCheckModifications

Previously, UncheckedIterator<T> included modification-tracking fields
and runtime checks in CheckModifications() whenever either
ENABLE_VECTOR_MODIFICATION_CHECKS or
ENABLE_HEAP_VECTOR_MODIFICATION_CHECKS was enabled at build time, even
for Vector/HeapVector instantiations where kEnableModificationChecks
was false. In out-of-line STL algorithms such as std::stable_sort and
std::inplace_merge (e.g. LogicalLineBuilder::BidiReorder on
HeapVector<LogicalLineItem>), this enlarged the iterator from 8 bytes
to 16 bytes and prevented the compiler from eliding null checks on
modifications_ptr_.

Parameterize UncheckedIterator<T, bool kCheckModifications> on
kEnableModificationChecks so disabled vector types use a pointer-sized
iterator with zero modification-tracking state or runtime checks.

TAG=agy
CONV=faa0d6f3-6c3b-4254-a2f2-3f8e82f4004a

[rust] Share `build_bindgen.py`'s way of running `cargo`.

This CL moves the generic part of `RunCargo` from `build_bindgen.py`
into `GetHostCargoEnv` and `RunHostCargo` in `host_tools.py`.
`build_bindgen.py` keeps only its own settings (`LLVM_CONFIG_PATH`,
`LIBCLANG_*`, ncursesw).  No behavior change is intended.

A follow-up CL will use the helpers in `build_crubit.py`, instead of
`//tools/crates/run_cargo.py`.  This gives the same toolchain and
the same (hermetic, via `setenv=True`) MSVC environment on Windows as
for `bindgen`.

Resources.NotFoundException because the test's font-family XML had no
android:font attribute, so the platform Font.Builder path introduced
by TypefaceCompatApi29Impl received resource id 0. Point the font
entry at a real font file (a copy of third_party/test_fonts
GardinerModCat.ttf) and re-enable the test.

[ChroMenu] Implement SearchResults categorization and search result tree

Implements BuildSearchResults() and BuildSearchResultsTree() to
partition FuzzyFinder matches into category sections (Actions,

caps, and construct an ephemeral ActionItem tree for rendering search
results (or a disabled empty-state item when no results match).

[rust] Share host toolchain and CMake settings between build scripts.

* `build.py`: Add `GetThirdPartyCMakeArgs`, used by `BuildLibXml2` and
  `BuildZStd`.  No change in behavior.
* `host_tools.py` (new): Add helpers that return the compilers, the
  sysroot flags, and the linker settings for host tools that link
  the LLVM libraries from `RUST_HOST_LLVM_INSTALL_DIR`.
* `build_rust.py`: Move the Mac SDK lookup into `GetMacSdkPath` (also
  used by `host_tools.py`).
* `build_bindgen.py`: Use the new helpers from `host_tools.py`.
  Changes in behavior:
  - The Debian sysroot is not downloaded again - it comes from the
    earlier `build_rust.py` run.
  - `AR` is set to `llvm-ar` (`llvm-lib` on Windows), like in
    `build_rust.py`.

`build_crubit.py` will use these helpers in follow-up CLs: the linker
settings to link `cc_bindings_from_rs`, and the compilers and CMake args
to build `rs_bindings_from_cc` and its C++ dependencies (Abseil,
Protobuf).

OIDC: Fix invalid downcast in OidcAuthenticationSigninInterceptorTest

OidcAuthenticationSigninInterceptorTest instantiated interceptor_ as an
instance of OidcAuthenticationSigninInterceptor, but tests
static_cast-ed it to MockOidcAuthenticationSigninInterceptor to call
test helpers. This invalid downcast caused CFI and UBSan (vptr) failures
on Linux bots.

This CL moves the testing helpers (SetNewProfileForTesting and
FinalizeSigninInterceptionForTesting) directly to the base class
OidcAuthenticationSigninInterceptor, eliminates the illegal downcasts,
and re-enables the disabled tests.

Don't rebuild date-time edit fields when layout parameters are unchanged.

The primary change here is changing DateTimeEditElement::GetLayout to
return early if the layout parameters are unchanged.  However, this
change has a number of prerequisites that are also included here:

* Adds default comparison operators to make it possible to compare
  LayoutParameters objects.

* Moves the needs-millisecond-field information into the
  LayoutParameters.

* Recompute style when changing values (in cases where, previously,
  elements were reconstructed, plus SetValueAsDateTimeFieldsState which
  was likely buggy) so that GetCustomStyleForLayoutObject will rerun
  when the value changes, since it depends on the value (e.g., setting a
  different width for 5-digit years).

* Clear cached type-ahead buffers when changing the values (which
  reconstructing the elements previously did, except in the
  SetValueAsDateTimeFieldsState case).

Revert "[macOS] Add prevent_stale_content_after_hide widget flag"

This reverts commit 9343a0b691f16b5b0fe4a23e076e4f75ca741c04.

Reason for revert: Enabling this flag resulted in the view we enabled it
for sometimes not showing up if it was shown at exactly the same size.
For now we ended up with https://crrev.com/c/8397857 and will revisit
this if needed.

Original change's description:
> [macOS] Add prevent_stale_content_after_hide widget flag
>
> When kAlphaInsteadOfCATransaction is enabled, a window's alpha is set to
> 0 while waiting for its initial compositor frame in order to prevent
> visual/rendering issues. This is only applied on the initial show and
> not for subsequent shows.
>
> This CL adds a new `prevent_stale_content_after_hide` Widget option to
> enable addressing cases where it is desirable to use the same alpha
> technique for subsequent show/hide events.
>
> The primary/current use case for this is Omnibox WebUI which has
> different display semantics than normal tabs/windows. The Omnibox caches
> windows/widgets for efficiency, but never wants to be shown with
> old/stale content from previous displays while waiting for new WebUI
> compositor frames to render. This change will enable the removal of
> several hacks currently in place for the AI mode Omnibox as well as
> stabilize the show/presentation of both the Full WebUI and AI Mode
> Omnibox when the Full WebUI Omnibox is enabled.
>
> Note that enabling eliminates stale frames stale frames when showing
> after a hide at the cost of waiting for the next frame to be produced
> before showing. This may make sense for ephemeral UI that is always
> displayed with new state (ex. Omnibox) but be less advantageous in
> scenarios where showing stale content faster will seem more responsive
> (eg. browser window).
>
> This CL:
>
> 1. Adds `prevent_stale_content_after_hide` to `Widget::InitParams`
>    and `NativeWidgetNSWindowInitParams`.
> 2. Adds `should_reset_alpha_on_show_` in `NativeWidgetNSWindowBridge`,
>    which is set on hide when `prevent_stale_content_after_hide`
>    is enabled and cleared when a matching compositor frame arrives.
> 3. Updates show logic to zero window alpha when
>    `should_reset_alpha_on_show_` is set until the new frame is received.
> 4. Adds unit test coverage in native_widget_mac_unittest.mm.
>
> TAG=agy
> CONV=b6cd62f8-b9fd-44dc-b919-81e10b6ae430
>

> Change-Id: Ife50f65dd4367947159254fea8a13f1c3b1dfaea

Checked Span: Place tests in fixture

The tests are currently written to rely on PartitionAlloc-Everywhere
support. Although PA-E is widely deployed, there's no particular reason
to gate Checked Span tests on it. This CL places Checked Span tests in a
fixture that avails a dedicated PartitionAlloc instance for use.

Additionally, relying directly on PA-E hides the PartitionAllocator
instance from the test authors and prevents them from writing richer
tests, e.g. ones that may check if BackupRefPtr is enabled. Gating on
this is required to properly test Checked Span's "smuggled size"
feature.

One behavioral change: `UncheckedSpanNeverCrashes` is modified not to
bother checking that the test allocation doesn't fill a slot, which is
irrelevant to the demonstration of `base::unchecked` (and crashy in
sanitizer builds).

This CL was generated with Jetski (and touched up by hand).

52d57362a5f2153912e841b44ed72846f3760f87 [ diff ] 
CORS: Do not cache preflight responses with certificate errors

Previously, PreflightController::PreflightLoader cached CORS preflight
responses in PreflightCache for up to 2 hours without checking
URLResponseHead::cert_status. If a user clicked through a certificate
error interstitial for a host and an active network attacker answered a
preflight request, the cross-origin authorization was cached and
persisted even after the MITM ended and the certificate exception was
revoked upon receiving a valid certificate.

Consistent with other persistence and caching mechanisms in Chromium
(such as HSTS, Alt-Svc, NEL, DBSC, and Use-As-Dictionary in
CorsURLLoader), allow the individual request's preflight check to pass
when net::IsCertStatusError(head.cert_status) is true (preserving
compatibility with self-signed certificates in local development
environments), but skip storing the result in PreflightCache.

Also inline FinishHandleResponseHeader() into HandleResponseHeader() now
that it is only called synchronously at the end of
HandleResponseHeader().

DomStorage: Preserve sessionStorage for session restore

When the last browser window closes, SessionService keeps its tabs in
the saved session so they can be restored on the next launch. However,
SessionServiceBase::TabClosing() marked each tab's sessionStorage
namespace as non-persistent. As a result, when the final namespace
handle was destroyed, the Storage Service deleted the namespace's
sessionStorage data, leaving the restored tab with empty sessionStorage.

This change adds a virtual ShouldDeleteSessionStorageOnTabClosing() to
SessionServiceBase. The default implementation preserves the existing
behavior for services such as AppSessionService. SessionService
overrides it to keep namespaces for windows in
pending_window_close_ids_, allowing their backing data to survive for
session restore.

[History] Route chrome://history navigations to WebUI on Android

Android navigations to chrome://history are currently handled by
native Java UI (HistoryManager and HistoryPage).

This change registers HistoryUIConfig in content::WebUIConfig on
Android, rewrites chrome-native://history to chrome://history in
the URL handler, and introduces the WebUiHistory feature flag. When
enabled, NativePage returns NONE for history hosts, and
HistoryManagerUtils launches chrome://history in a standard tab.

[BottomSheet] Remove duplicate margin subtraction in getMaxSheetHeight

Since mSheetContainer's bottomMargin already shrinks mContainerHeight by
the effective bottom margin (including the 24dp desktop bottom margin in
DESKTOP_POPUP mode), getMaxSheetHeight() only needs to subtract the top
desktop gap (mDesktopBottomMargin) rather than subtracting
getContainerBottomMargin() a second time.

[IAU 2/4] Add snackbar controllers and telemetry for In-App Updates

Chrome on Android is introducing support for Google Play In-App Updates
to allow seamless background downloads and restart prompts without
redirecting users to the external Play Store application.

See "Important Note On Prototype" at http://shortn/_Gc3KVC8Pzk (design
doc section)

This CL implements the dedicated UI controllers, string resources, and
telemetry for the in-app update snackbars:

- InAppUpdateSnackbarController.java: Displays a notification
  snackbar informing users that an update is available, with an
  "Update" action to initiate a flexible background download, and
  when a background update has finished downloading, with a
  "Restart" action to relaunch Chrome and complete the update.
- Decoupled UI architecture: Converts Play Core calls into injected
  Runnable callbacks (onAccept, optional onDismiss), keeping the UI
  layer fully decoupled from Play Core dependencies.
- Throttle integration: onDismissNoAction triggers
  InAppUpdatePolicy.recordUpdateDeclined() (discovery) or
  InAppUpdatePolicy.recordRestartDeclined() (restart), ensuring passive
  timeouts properly pace subsequent prompts.

See http://shortn/_l3smgQZB0m for design context and state diagrams.

This is part 2 of the in-app update CL series. Subsequent CLs will wire
these controllers into InAppUpdateController and ChromeActivity.

[Linux] Support XDG NetworkMonitor portal in NetworkChangeNotifierLinux

Connect NetworkChangeNotifierLinux to the XDG Desktop Portal
org.freedesktop.portal.NetworkMonitor interface over D-Bus when
USE_DBUS is enabled:
- Query connection metering and online status via GetStatus (portal v3+)
  or GetMetered/GetAvailable (portal v2), and listen to the 'changed'
  signal and NameOwnerChanged for updates.
- Override GetCurrentConnectionCost() to return CONNECTION_COST_METERED
  or CONNECTION_COST_UNMETERED and notify observers when the effective
  cost changes.
- Behind kNetworkChangeNotifierPortalOnlineState (disabled by default),
  incorporate portal online/offline state into
  GetCurrentConnectionType() so offline portal state reports
  CONNECTION_NONE and online portal state upgrades netlink
  CONNECTION_NONE to CONNECTION_UNKNOWN.
- Add unit tests for v3, v2 fallback, feature-disabled default behavior,
  and late portal startup / service owner reset interactions.

blobs in the Contacts Picker with out-of-process image decoding via

[WebRTC] Migrate video detection in browsertests to video_frame_detector.js

This CL modernizes video detection across WebRTC and capture
browsertests by replacing the legacy `video_detector.js` with
`video_frame_detector.js`.

The legacy `video_detector.js` drew frames to an offscreen 2D canvas
every 100ms and computed a pixel sum fingerprint across a 5-sample
sliding window. For static video content (such as self-capture in
getDisplayMedia or desktop captures), pixel values stabilize rapidly,
causing `isVideoPlaying()` to fail to detect video changes and
intermittently time out on bots.

`video_frame_detector.js` tracks delivered video frames using
`HTMLVideoElement.requestVideoFrameCallback()` and
`HTMLVideoElement.getVideoPlaybackQuality().totalVideoFrames`. This
reliably detects playback in both foreground and background tabs without
relying on artificial pixel differences.

This removes `video_detector.js` and migrates all referencing HTML test
pages and C++ browsertest fixtures to `video_frame_detector.js`.

[BottomSheet] Rename BottomSheet to BottomSheetCoordinator

In the preceding MVC refactoring CLs, BottomSheet was decoupled from the
Android View hierarchy (with layout roots and view rendering moved to
BottomSheetView and state/gesture logic moved to BottomSheetMediator).
Because BottomSheet is no longer a View subclass and instead acts as the
MVC Coordinator that owns and wires together BottomSheetView,
BottomSheetMediator, and the PropertyModel, rename it to
BottomSheetCoordinator to reflect its architectural role.

Also rename BottomSheetUnitTest to BottomSheetCoordinatorUnitTest so the
unit test suite is easy to locate alongside BottomSheetCoordinator, and
update internal callers, factory hooks, and test helpers accordingly.

[WebCodecs] Create flush() promises in the caller's realm

Audio and video encoders and decoders created the promise returned by
`flush()` using the `ScriptState` captured at construction. When
`flush()` was called from a different world or realm than the one that
created the codec, the caller received a promise belonging to the
creator's realm.

Add `[CallWith=ScriptState]` to `flush()` and create the resolver with
the caller's `ScriptState`, so the returned promise always belongs to
the caller. Calls from the creating realm are unaffected. Output and
error callbacks keep using the creator's `ScriptState`, since they are
registered by the creator.

TAG=agy
CONV=ed044e08-4c4f-4368-b71d-4f1cc33142b8

[OpenScreen] Fail fast when the perf sender DUT is unreachable

The mediarouter-perf bots drive a remote sender over SSH. When the
sender was down, failed SSH commands were treated as empty output, so
runs failed much later with misleading errors such as
"Unsupported OS/Arch: mac/", picked win32 Chrome after guessing x86, and
logged false successes ("Old chromedriver processes confirmed gone",
"Cleaned up remote Chrome/Chromedriver directories").

This change:
- Adds verify_sender_connectivity(), which checks DNS, TCP port 22, and
  `echo ok` over SSH, with 3 attempts 5s apart. The result is cached
  per process. Failures raise a RemoteDeviceError subclass
  (SenderNotFoundError, SenderUnreachableError, SenderSshError) that
  says it is an infra failure, not a test failure.
- Calls it before any remote work: setup_test_environment,
  get_remote_info, terminate_old_chromedriver, install_and_setup_chrome,
  setup_cros_environment, and start_ssh_tunnel.
- Adds BatchMode=yes and ConnectTimeout=10 to ssh/scp, and logs an
  ERROR when ssh exits 255.
- Removes the silent fallbacks: an unknown Windows arch no longer
  becomes x86, empty arch/os_version raises, and a 255 from the
  chromedriver check raises instead of reading as "gone".
- Skips remote cleanup once the sender is known to be unreachable, and
  logs "Cleaned up ..." only when the command succeeded.
- Adds common_unittest.py and a PRESUBMIT.py that runs it.

This reverts commit ad298cb0b496261782101f1c647945e65df7ad6e.

Reason for revert: Reland with the fix for the CHECK failure.

Differences from the original reland CL:
Removed CHECK_NE(history_offset, 0) in RecordInitiatorMetrics() so that
when a reload navigation is served from BFCache
(https://crbug.com/420769973) with history_offset == 0, it falls through
to the subsequent checks and is classified as kReload.

Reland "[PDF] Scrollbar glow up"

This reverts commit 7e46a5ed54e63a1ac88897bd41e24b2edcc18da8.

Reason for revert: The problem was loading too many thumbnails due to
the layout change for the thumbnails sidebar.

The fix is to set height:100% and to include the scrollbar styles in the
thumbnails bar lit element. In the initial land the thumbnails bar got
height:auto implicitly when I changed it to display:block which caused
all of the thumbnails to count as visible and made the parent div scroll
instead of scrolling internally in the thumbnails bar as it was supposed
to.

Alternatively I could have included the scrollbar CSS and left the
thumbnail bar as display:inline which implicitly inherits the
height:100% but I think it's more semantically accurate to consider the
thumbnails bar to be a block element.

There is now a generic regression test that can detect loading too many
thumbnails (added in the parent CL).

Original change's description:
> Revert "[PDF] Scrollbar glow up"
>
> This reverts commit 0168036725890c6c62dfded69dabed8871d59bae.
>
> Reason for revert: Caused performance problems with too many thumbnails getting loaded.
>
> Failure Link: crbug.com/565684021
>
> Original change's description:
> > [PDF] Scrollbar glow up
> >
> > Removes the white background for the scrollbar track on Linux and
> > Windows. This CL also overrides the default MacOS scrollbars which have
> > no track and disappear. Previously on MacOS some of the scrollbars were
> > badly colored dark-on-dark because of the dark mode situation with the
> > PDF viewer. Now all platforms have the same look.
> >
> > The left sidebar scrolls inside the lit elements so set the scrollbar
> > styles on the parent sidenav element. It was also necessary to set the
> > 3 potential left sidenav elements to display:block otherwise the
> > scrollbar styles don't apply. The outline and attachments views were
> > already set to display:block in the same way via a :host selected so
> > this CL only sets the thumbnails view to display:block (the others also
> > had some padding but I didn't add that to thumbnails).
> >
> > The right sidebar (the tools for text and drawing) scroll from outside
> > the lit element instead as a child of <pdf-viewer>, so set the scrollbar
> > styles in pdf_viewer.css for the right sidebar. This also catches any
> > other top-level elements that might end up with a scrollbar in the
> > future and is the location of the javascript scrollbar width check.
> >
> > For the main PDF view it is necessary to set the styles in
> > plugin_response_writer.cc since this view is buried deep in a <embed>
> > tag shadow dom. The scroll element is the <html> inside the top-level
> > <embed>. There is a special case for print preview because that is the
> > only PDF UI that responds to dark/light mode changes. So it's necessary
> > to set the track color to white in light mode to make the print preview
> > look good. This styling also affects PDFs <iframe>'d into another page.
> > Also note that the body background-color in pdf/index.css is the color
> > behind the scrollbars for the PDF content as the tracks are set to
> > transparent.
> >
> > TAG=agy

[TabModel] Migrate TabGroupObserver.didCreateNewGroup to Token

TabGroupObserver.didCreateNewGroup previously passed a representative
destination Tab even though the group Token is already resolved at the
dispatch site in TabCollectionTabModelImpl. Pass the group Token
directly to decouple group creation notifications from representative
Tab instances, and split ModelTrackingOrchestrator's visual data
observer into regular and incognito instances so each observer knows
whether its model is incognito without inspecting a Tab.

[CRD] Restore video capturer settings after desktop reattach

When the desktop process is restarted, DesktopSessionProxy requests a
new capturer from it, and IpcVideoFrameCapturer only calls Start() on
it. The new capturer's frame scheduler starts with a max frame rate of
0 and doesn't schedule any capture until it gets a non-zero frame rate.
WebRTC only calls SetMaxFrameRate() when its constraints change, so the
video stays frozen while the cursor keeps updating. The same applies to
the new capturer created by SelectSource().

Make IpcVideoFrameCapturer cache the compose, max frame rate and pause
settings, and send them right after Start() whenever a capturer is
started, including on new Mojo endpoints. Settings set before Start()
are now only cached, since the scheduler ignores a frame rate received
before Start().

Also fix comments claiming OnDisconnect() replies to pending frame
requests.

[VideoCapture] Remove unsafe lifetime assumptions in InProcessVideoCaptureDeviceLauncher

InProcessVideoCaptureDeviceLauncher assumed that the caller-provided
done_cb extended the lifetime of this until asynchronous device launch
completed. It also posted base::Unretained(this) across threads to the
device task runner and bound base::Unretained(this) for the IO-thread
completion callback.

This CL refactors InProcessVideoCaptureDeviceLauncher to manage its own
lifetime safety:

1. Bind weak_factory_.GetWeakPtr() to OnDeviceStarted on the IO thread
so callbacks drop safely if the launcher is destroyed before launch
completes.

2. Convert device-thread helper methods to static methods with explicit
arguments, eliminating cross-thread base::Unretained(this) passing.

3. Remove fake_device_factory_ member from the launcher instance,
passing it to OnFakeDevicesEnumerated directly.

4. Remove dead declaration
DoStartDesktopCaptureWithReceiverOnDeviceThread.

Pad silence in MFAudioEncoder on flush when input is too short

The Media Foundation AAC Encoder MFT (mfAACEnc.dll) maintains a 2-frame
(2,048 samples) internal lookahead/delay buffer and requires at least
that many samples in its pipeline before MFT_MESSAGE_COMMAND_DRAIN can
successfully resolve and drain the final frame.

Previously, MFAudioEncoder tracked `can_flush_` and rejected Flush()
calls with `kEncoderFailedFlush` if fewer than 2 frames had been
provided. This caused short audio streams (< 43 ms) to fail on Windows,
introducing an inconsistent platform limitation compared to macOS,
Android, and Opus encoders which handle short inputs cleanly.

This CL updates MFAudioEncoder::Flush() to insert a silent AudioBus when
the total pending samples in the pipeline are > 0 and < 2 frames. This
satisfies the MFT's drain requirement and allows the final frame(s) to
be emitted successfully.

Unit tests are updated to remove the Windows-specific flush failure
expectation and verify short input flushes across all platforms.

Fix CloseWebContents DUMP_WILL_BE_NOTREACHED during shutdown

If an individual tab is already closing when browser shutdown begins
(e.g. pressing Cmd+W, Cmd+Q, Cmd+Q in quick succession on macOS), the
tab finishing its unload calls BrowserWebContentsDelegate::CloseContents
which checks UnloadController::CanCloseContents() before calling
chrome::CloseWebContents().

Despite its query-like name, CanCloseContents() has side effects:
clearing that tab's unload state can synchronously complete the browser
window close and detach all tabs from the tab strip. CanCloseContents()
would then inspect the already-detached tab and return true, causing
CloseWebContents() to be called for a tab no longer in the tab strip.

Fix this by:
- Checking the UnloadController state in CanCloseContents() before
  looking up the tab in the tab strip, returning false once the window
  is closing.
- Upgrading DUMP_WILL_BE_NOTREACHED() in CloseWebContents() to CHECK_NE
  and adding a regression test.

[Omnibox] Gate CachedZeroSuggestionsManager on feature flag

Ensure CachedZeroSuggestionsManager is not invoked at all when
ServeJavaCachedZeroSuggest is disabled:
- Return false in AutocompleteInput#isInCacheableContext() when the
feature is disabled, preventing
LocationBarMediator#beginOrResumeInput,
AutocompleteMediator#serveCachedZeroSuggest, and
AutocompleteMediator#maybeCacheResult from invoking the cache.
- Guard all read/write/clear entry points in
CachedZeroSuggestionsManager and
AutocompleteMediator#onPauseWithNative behind
OmniboxFeatures.sServeJavaCachedZeroSuggest.isEnabled().

Reland "[TopControls] Read the toolbar's capture offset instead of deriving it"

This is a reland of commit 8352a57b3ad27521fe4ca85f1fabd758157fda57

Before: http://go/scrcast/NTkxMDk2MzExODE0NTUzNnwyYjJiZTkzZi0yZg
After: http://go/scrcast/NjYxNTMxNjQ4MTE3OTY0OHxjNTJlMGUwMC1lZA

Original change's description:
> [TopControls] Read the toolbar's capture offset instead of deriving it
>
> Read the toolbar's capture offset instead of deriving it.
> -Previously, we would use properties of views in the control container
>  to determine how much to offset the capture to correctly position the
>  toolbar.
> -However, we already directly measure where the toolbar lives in its
>  parent container when capturing the snapshot. We can use this exact
>  value instead of deriving from the surrounding views.
> -More than just a cleanup, this is also a speculative fix for issues
>  that seem to come from "off-by-one" rounding errors in the dp->px
>  conversions between both views and the captured snapshot.
>

Migrate ChromeShelfController browser-using tests to browser_tests

Migrate all tests in chrome_shelf_controller_unittest.cc that actually
require a Browser or TabStripModel instance to
chrome_shelf_controller_browsertest.cc:
- Single-profile tests (BrowserMenuGeneration, V1AppMenu*,
  PersistShelfItemPositions, PersistPinned,
  ExistingBrowserWindowShelfIDSet) are moved to ShelfAppBrowserTest and
  ShelfAppBrowserTestNoDefaultBrowser.
- Multi-profile browser/window tests (V1AppUpdateOnUserSwitch*,
  V1CloseOnVisitingDesktop, TestShelfActivationPullsBackWindow,
  WebAppNotShownIfNotInstalledAfterUserSwitch,
  BrowserMenuGenerationTwoUsers, V1AppMenuGenerationTwoUsers) are moved
  to a new ShelfMultiProfileBrowserTest fixture.

Update remaining unit tests in chrome_shelf_controller_unittest.cc that
trivially accessed browser()->GetProfile() or
InitShelfControllerWithBrowser() to use profile() and
InitShelfController() directly, and remove unused browser helper classes
and functions.

[Windows] Implement Small Gesture Writing for Stylus Handwriting [3/4]

See Part 1 (CL:8262960) for the full feature summary.
See Part 2 (CL:8266203) for changes to ui to expose pixels-per-inch.

Part 3 implements the physical-distance movement threshold for
handwriting:
  * Latch per-axis PPI and device scale at TouchStart.
  * Convert movement to HIMETRIC and apply a field-trial-controlled threshold.
  * Propagate the initiating device PPI through
RenderWidgetHostViewInput.
  * Start handwriting after the configurable movement threshold,
    ShowPress, and writable touch-action requirements are satisfied.
  * Allow GestureTap to support low-movement characters such as
punctuation.

Lifecycle changes such as handling terminating gestures are
intentionally left for part 4 of these changes.

[WebUI] Do not close cr-action-menu on drag release inside dialog

When pressing mouse down on one slotted menu item and releasing
mouse up on a different slotted menu item in cr-action-menu, the
browser dispatches the click event on their lowest common
ancestor, which is the cr-action-menu host element itself
(e.target === this). Previously, onClick_ treated any click with
e.target === this as a backdrop click and closed the menu.

Disable caret blinking in WPT runs

Caret blinking causes flaky test failures for those that capture
screenshots, so is already disabled by `LayoutTheme::CaretBlinkInterval`
when in web test mode. WPTs don't run in web test mode, however, so were
still susceptible to this failure unless they individually set
`caret-animation: manual`. Though many of the caret-focused tests do
this already, many other tests include a caret and do not know they need
to set such a style.

This change adds a flag to control the blinking caret and disables it
for desktop WPT runs, broadly improving their flakiness.

Though many tests were found that this is expected to improve, none of
them are currently flaky enough to have been disabled.

dec5337aa7c8484a5c82d03e2b283b3e446a6a1a [ diff ] 
[CRD] Hop clipboard events to DesktopSessionAgent's thread

DesktopSessionClipboardStub called DesktopSessionAgent directly,
assuming the clipboard runs on the agent's thread. That holds for
ClipboardWin and the Wayland clipboards, but ClipboardX11 runs on the
input thread. Once X events are dispatched in the desktop process,
copying text on the host hits a DCHECK in
DesktopSessionAgent::OnClipboardEvent() (or races in release builds).

Wrap the agent's clipboard stub in ClipboardThreadProxy, like
PeerSessionImpl does. To avoid a redundant same-thread hop on both sides
of the IPC, ClipboardThreadProxy now calls the stub directly when it is
already on the stub's sequence.

5a47a9c56685e47307b81af8dd8e8556c31e4b5b [ diff ] 
[tracing] Let TracingControllerImpl start from a perfetto config

TracingController::StartTracing() builds its perfetto config internally
with GetDefaultPerfettoConfig() and always asks for the legacy JSON
conversion. Callers that want the raw protobuf trace, or that want to
record a data source with no base::trace_event::TraceConfig
representation -- for example Chromium's trace-scoped native heap
profiler -- have to run a second perfetto::TracingSession alongside the
shared one, so those samples land in a different trace from everything
else.

This CL adds a method to TracingControllerImpl that takes a
perfetto::TraceConfig directly:

bool StartTracingWithPerfettoConfig(const perfetto::TraceConfig&,
                                      StartTracingDoneCallback);

Callers assemble the config themselves, starting from
tracing::GetDefaultPerfettoConfig() if they want the usual data sources.
The content/public API is unchanged apart from a comment.

The output format follows the config. If its data sources set
convert_to_legacy_json, the session behaves as before and calls
DisableTracingAndEmitJson(). Otherwise the trace is delivered as the raw
protobuf: the session calls DisableTracing() and reads the buffers with
ReadBuffers() once OnTracingDisabled() has arrived, since a data source
may still be emitting its final samples while it is disabled.

convert_to_legacy_json applies to the whole session -- ConsumerHost
turns the conversion on if any data source asks for it -- so a config
whose data sources disagree is rejected.

Two consequences worth calling out:

 * |agent_label| filters the converted JSON, so StopTracing() rejects
   a non-empty label for a protobuf trace.

 * IsTracing() no longer keys off |trace_config_|, which is null for a
   session started from a perfetto config, and the "update the process
   filter of a running session" path now requires |trace_config_|.

FileTraceDataEndpoint now opens its FILE* in binary mode. It can receive
payloads that are not text -- gzip data when CompressedTraceDataEndpoint
is chained onto it, and now protobuf traces -- and Windows text mode
translates '\n' to '\r\n', corrupting them. The gzip case is reachable
today but has no in-tree caller.

Enforce cross-origin access control in WebUIURLLoaderFactory

WebUIURLLoaderFactory is a non-network factory, so subresource requests
handled by it do not go through the CORS checks applied by the network
service. Consequently, requests between chrome-untrusted:// origins were
processed without validating whether the target data source permits
cross-origin access via
URLDataSource::GetAccessControlAllowOriginForOrigin().

This change binds the requesting initiator origin lock to the factory at
creation time and validates cross-origin requests from
chrome-untrusted:// initiators against the target data source's access
control configuration. Relevant data sources such as shared resources,
webui-test, theme, and favicon2 are updated to explicitly declare their
permitted cross-origin access.

TAG=agy

Change base::Location to store uintptr_t instead of void*

Change `base::Location::program_counter_` from raw_ptr<const void,
UnprotectedInRelease> to uintptr_t, and update base::Location to use
uintptr_t.

A program counter is an instruction address in the executable code
segment rather than a PartitionAlloc heap allocation, and it is never
dereferenced. Using raw_ptr provides no UAF protection and previously
required the UnprotectedInRelease annotation to avoid performance
overhead. Storing it as uintptr_t better reflects its semantics as an
opaque address value.

Update code that interacts with base::Location to use uintptr_t, and
remove casts in code that needed uintptr_t anyway. Stop short of
converting base::StackTrace to use uintptr_t. Instead, just add a new
base::StackTrace ctor to take a span of uintptr_ts.

[actor] Show preparing snackbar on external trigger fallback

When Glic is externally triggered while background actuation is
disabled (e.g. when system notifications are disabled), Chrome falls
back to foregrounding ChromeTabbedActivity with a trusted
EXTRA_GLIC_PENDING_ACTOR_TASK intent.

This CL:
1. Introduces ActorExternalTriggerSnackbarController (owned by
   GlicUiCoordinator) to display a persistent "Preparing to start your
   task…" snackbar (Snackbar.UMA_ACTOR_EXTERNAL_TRIGGER) when
   ChromeTabbedActivity handles a trusted pending actor task trigger on
   cold start or warm start (onNewIntentWithNative).
2. Defers showing the snackbar until onStartWithNative() if the trigger
   intent arrives while the activity is still stopped and
   SnackbarManager#canShowSnackbar() is false.
3. Observes ActorKeyedService on the regular profile
   (profile.getOriginalProfile()) and dismisses the snackbar as soon as
   a task is created (ActorTaskState.CREATED).

[Toolbar] Restore BROWSING layout after closing last tab in LocationBarModelTest

In LocationBarModelTest, testClosingLastTabReflectedInModel closes the
last open tab, which triggers LayoutManagerChrome.tabClosed ->
showLayout(LayoutType.HUB, true). On tablets and desktop form factors
(LayoutManagerChromeTablet), when AutoResetCtaTransitTestRule opens a
new tab for the next test in the @Batch(Batch.PER_CLASS) suite,
mNextActiveLayout remains LayoutType.HUB and mStaticLayout stays
isStartingToHide(), causing the compositor to transition to HUB and fail
WebPageStation entry.

Restore a tab and wait for LayoutType.BROWSING at the end of
testClosingLastTabReflectedInModel.

[CRD Linux] Dispatch X events in the desktop process

The desktop process never created a ui::X11EventSource, so X events on
the per-thread x11::Connection were only dispatched when some other
code happened to call DispatchAll() (e.g. DesktopResizerX11). As a
result, DesktopDisplayInfoLoaderX11 missed RANDR events and newly added
monitors were not reported to the client until reconnecting. X11
clipboard and keyboard layout monitoring were affected too.

Add ThreadBoundX11EventSource, which owns an X11EventSource for the
current thread and deletes itself right before the thread's message
loop is destroyed, so it doesn't need to be deleted explicitly.

In the desktop process, use a UI message pump for the input thread on
Linux and create a ThreadBoundX11EventSource on the main and input
threads. In the single-process host, replace the manually managed
X11EventSources with ThreadBoundX11EventSource, and do the same in the
It2Me native messaging host. The multi-process network process no
longer creates them, since X11 is only used by the desktop process.

[Contextual Tasks] Test ephemeral button reopen

Adds an interactive UI test covering the Ephemeral Toolbar Button
Reopen journey for Contextual Tasks across all user variations
(signed-in, signed-out, and incognito) to ensure end-to-end
functionality and protect against regressions.

This tests the following CUJ:
 (1) User navigates to a webpage and starts a Lens region search from
     the Chrome app menu.
 (2) Contextual Tasks side panel opens with an active task for the tab.
 (3) User clicks the close button in the Contextual Tasks side panel
     toolbar.
 (4) Side panel closes and the ephemeral Contextual Tasks button
     appears in the browser toolbar.
 (5) User clicks the ephemeral toolbar button.
 (6) Contextual Tasks side panel reopens and restores the same task and
     side panel contents.
 (7) Ephemeral toolbar button hides while the side panel is open.

Key Implementation Details:
- User Variations: New ContextualTasksEphemeralToolbarInteractiveUiTest
  fixture derives from the UserVariation-parameterized
  ContextualTasksInteractiveUiTest and runs across kSignedIn,
  kSignedOut, and kIncognito.
- Real User Entry Points: The side panel is opened through the Lens
  overlay region search (app menu -> Lens -> region drag), closed via
  the WebUI toolbar #closeButton, and reopened by pressing the
  ephemeral toolbar button. No internal Show()/Close() calls are used.
- Isolated Flags: The fixture enables
  kContextualTasksEphemeralBrandedEntryPoint (toolbar-ephemeral-branded,
  with the right-hand button variant so the button does not depend on
  the default side panel alignment) and
  kContextualTasksForceEntryPointEligibility without leaking them into
  other suites in the file.
- Rehydration Checks: Verifies the active tab keeps the same task ID
  across close/reopen and that the reopened panel reuses the cached
  side panel WebContents.
- Anti-Flakiness: Side panel animations are disabled by the base
  fixture, the close button is waited on with non-zero layout bounds
  before clicking, the close click uses kFireAndForget since the
  clicked WebUI hides in response, and the side panel WebView is
  re-instrumented under a fresh identifier after reopening.

Verification:
- Local: 20/20 consecutive passes per variation via tools/autotest.py
  --gtest_repeat=20 (60/60 runs total)
- Swarm: 10 bots via tools/run-swarmed.py --copies 10 with
  --gtest_repeat=5; 50/50 passes per variation (150/150 runs total),
  0 flakes

[Boca] Prevent OAuth query marker bypass under BLOCK_NAVIGATION

In OnTaskLockedSessionNavigationThrottle, CheckRestrictions() previously
evaluated IsOauthLoginComplete() and IsOauthLoginStart() before checking
the tab's URL blocklist. This allowed a student in an active OnTask
locked session with BLOCK_NAVIGATION enabled to bypass navigation
restrictions by navigating to any blocked URL containing either:
1. Completion query parameters (code, access_token, id_token) even when
   no OAuth login flow was in progress.
2. A bare client_id query parameter without required OAuth 2.0
   authorization request parameters (response_type).

This change:
1. Requires window_tracker->oauth_in_progress() to be true in
   CheckRestrictions() before allowing IsOauthLoginComplete() to bypass
   restrictions.
2. Tightens IsOauthLoginStart() to also require the response_type query
   parameter (per RFC 6749).
3. Adds an interactive UI regression test
   RejectStatelessOauthMarkersUnderBlockNavRestriction.

BUG=b:541544177
TEST=browser_tests --gtest_filter="*OnTaskLockedSessionNavigationThrottle*"

Support same-site RFH swaps when initial page scale is non-default

RenderDocument same-site RFH swaps on WebView used to cause some test
failures when navigating from pages with initial page scale. This
CL adds a fix for that case, and rremoves the restriction in
AwContentBrowserClient that blocked same-site RenderFrameHost swaps
when initial_page_scale_is_non_default.

To fix test failures:
1. Preserve UserAgentConstraints (initial page scale) across main
   frame swaps in Page::TakePropertiesForLocalMainFrameSwap.
2. Guard InputHandler::UpdateRootLayerStateForSynchronousInputHandler
   to check InnerViewportScrollNode() before updating synchronous
   compositor scale, preventing uninitialized active trees from
    sending default (1.0f) scale.
3. Remove legacy ResetScrollAndScaleState call and
initial_page_scale_is_non_default_ state tracking from AwSettings.

Allow accessibility SetSelection to end at the end of a page.

Selection end indices are treated as exclusive, meaning that selecting up to the end of a page requires specifying the boundary immediately past the last character (equal to the page's character count). Previously, selection validation rejected this index because it required the index to reference an existing character.

Rename the validation helper to IsSelectionBoundaryInBounds() and allow the index to be equal to the character count, and add a test verifying selection to the end of a page.

[Omnibox] Clear omnibox focus in LocationBarTest#tearDown

LocationBarTest runs as @Batch(Batch.PER_CLASS) with
FreshCtaTransitTestRule, and several tests
(testOmniboxSearchEngineLogo_focusedOnSRP, testFocusCarriesSelection,
testEditingText) leave the UrlBar focused with the soft keyboard showing
when the test ends, without an @After tearDown() to clear focus. In
addition, testFocusLogic_keyboardVisibility and testFocusLogic_backPress
call mOmnibox.requestFocus() without waiting for focus animations to
complete before unfocusing.

Add an @After tearDown() method to clear omnibox focus and wait for
focus animations to complete after mOmnibox.requestFocus().

R=peterkang@google.com

[Reading mode PDFs] Name heuristic headings from their text contents

Per the ARIA specification, `role=heading` declares
`nameFrom: [contents, author]` with `nameRequired: true`, so a heading
must expose its text as its own accessible name. The PDF accessibility
tree builders only name the child `kStaticText` nodes, leaving the
`kHeading` node itself unnamed. On macOS this makes VoiceOver fall back
to the AXDisclosureLevel and announce "heading level 3, <text>,
level 2".

Add `PdfAccessibilityTreeBuilder::SetHeadingNameFromContents()` and call
it from both the heuristic and the structure tree builder once a heading
block's text is known. Roles such as `kParagraph` prohibit `nameFrom`
entirely, so only headings are named this way.

settings: Hide focus highlight on current pane title

The current pane title is focusable for accessibility, and receives
focus when scrolled into view. When not in touch mode (e.g. after
navigating to chrome://settings via the omnibox with a keyboard), it
drew the default focus highlight, which looks like a text selection.

Disable the default focus highlight on the non-interactive current
title. Clickable breadcrumb titles keep it.

Pair UserPerceivedLatencyOnCardSelection with its durations

Autofill.BetterAuth.UserPerceivedLatencyOnCardSelection.{OptedIn,OptedOut}
records whether the user had to wait for the preflight call response
after choosing a card, and pairs with the .OptedIn.Duration and
.OptedIn.TimedOutCvcFallback histograms that are emitted once the wait
ends. It was only logged when the risk-based authentication was
unavailable, because until now that was the only flow that waited.

The risk-based flow now waits as well when card-on-device verification
is enforced, and nearly all production traffic will take that flow. Left
as is, the duration histograms would receive samples while the base
event they are meant to be read against received none.

Log the base event whenever the flow can block on the preflight call
response. PreflightCallResponseReceivedOnCardSelection keeps being
logged for the risk-based flow so that its dashboards stay continuous
across the experiment.

[css] Reuse cached implicit scopes in parent frames

Implicit @scope traversal is cached via seen_implicit_scopes_, but this
wasn't being looked at when traversing parent frames. This adds some
logic to take this into account during parent frame traversal.

No behavioral changes are expected, just optimization:

ImplicitAtScopeInsertion -7.7%

ImplicitAtScope -2.7%

A WPT was added for sibling stylesheet @scope invalidation, which wasn't
currently covered.

Prevent Glic experimental triggering handler cleanup on self-superseded invocations.

Experimental triggering updates handlers are shared per context id, so a
continuation request invokes on the same handler that owns the in-flight
invocation it supersedes. GlicInvokeHandler::OnError() posts the
kSuperseded error asynchronously, so the handler previously tore itself
down (and stopped delivering updates) on the next task, even though the
continuation invocation was still in flight and waiting for updates.

Track the set of in-flight invocation IDs (`pending_invoke_ids_`) on
ExperimentalTriggeringUpdatesHandler, removing each ID in
OnInvokeSuccess() and OnInvokeError(), and ignore errors while another
invocation started by the same handler remains in flight.

[CustomTabs] Avoid Mockito.spy(CustomTabsConnection) in CustomTabActivityTest

CustomTabActivityTest#omniboxInCct_testInteractiveOmniboxOnEligibleCcts
used Mockito.spy(CustomTabsConnection.getInstance()) to stub
shouldEnableOmniboxForIntent(any()). Dynamically generating a DEX
subclass for CustomTabsConnection via AndroidByteBuddyMockMaker at
runtime on Android ART caused a SIGSEGV in dalvik-jit-code-cache
(net.bytebuddy.jar.asm.ByteVector.putByte).

Use a compile-time anonymous CustomTabsConnection subclass overriding
shouldEnableOmniboxForIntent(), and dismiss PageInfoController in
omniboxInCct_testNonInteractiveOmniboxWhenIntentNotEligible().

[Extensions] Keep global extension commands disabled on ChromeOS

crrev.com/c/8142000 added GlobalAcceleratorListenerChromeOS, so
ui::GlobalAcceleratorListener::GetInstance() is no longer null on
ChromeOS. ExtensionCommandsGlobalRegistry treats a non-null listener as
support for global commands, so extension global commands, which are
not supported on ChromeOS, started being registered with Ash.

This crashes when Chrome restarts inside a user session: the registry
is created with the user profile, which is then the initial profile,
and its extensions load before ChromeBrowserMainExtraPartsAsh::
PostProfileInit() creates MediaClientImpl. Registering a global media
key command then calls EnableCustomMediaKeyHandler() on a null
MediaClientImpl.

Don't use the GlobalAcceleratorListener for extension commands on
ChromeOS, which restores the behavior from before crrev.com/c/8142000.

[Glic] Reject non-file web drags in CanDragEnter and Invoke

Background: In production UMA, ~32% of
Glic.InvokeResult.WebDragDrop samples fail with
GlicInvokeError::kClipboardMissingMetadata (enum value 14, "Additional
context no clipboard metadata"). Manual testing reproduced this exact
failure when dragging a text hyperlink (<a>) from a web page (such as
Wikipedia) into Glic:
1. Blink populates DropData::url_infos and
   DropData::text for hyperlink drags, leaving DropData::file_contents
   empty (since file_contents is only populated for in-memory image/file
   payloads).
2. GlicView::CanDragEnter previously gated web drags on
   !data.url_infos.empty(), which allowed hyperlink drags (as well as
   cross-origin or broken image drags without accessible image bytes) to
   enter the Glic view and dispatch dragenter/dragover events to the
   Glic web client.
3. The Glic web client cannot filter out non-file web drags by checking
   for 'Files' in event.dataTransfer.types because on macOS,
   PopulateDropDataFromPasteboard (web_drag_dest_mac.mm) only populates
   drop_data.file_contents_source_url when a Content-Disposition pasteboard
   type is present, causing RenderWidgetHostImpl::DropDataToMetaData to
   omit the Binary ('Files') metadata item for standard web <img> drags.
   As a result, allowing dragenter/dragover caused the "Drop files here"
   overlay to appear when dragging hyperlinks.
4. On drop, StartDragAndDropInvoke constructed an AdditionalContext with
   a 0-byte ContextData buffer (drop_data.file_contents), which
   CopyPolicyTask::ExtractThumbnailData rejected (data->data.size() ==
   0), failing the invocation with
   GlicInvokeError::kClipboardMissingMetadata.

Fix:
- Temporarily gate web drags in GlicView::CanDragEnter on
  !data.file_contents.empty() instead of !data.url_infos.empty() so
  non-file web drags (such as hyperlinks) are rejected at drag-enter and
  never trigger the guest drop target overlay (tracked in b:567183211).
- Add a defense-in-depth check in StartDragAndDropInvoke to reject drops
  with empty file_contents early (recording
  GlicDragAndDropValidationResult::kUnsupportedContentType) before
  fetching page context or invoking GlicKeyedService::Invoke.
- Add unit tests (GlicViewTest.CanDragEnter,
  GlicViewTest.CanDragEnter_WebDragDisabled) and a browser regression
  test
  (GlicWebDragAndDropBrowserTest.testWebToGlicHyperlinkDragRejected).

Before: https://screencast.googleplex.com/cast/NjY5NDE1Mzc5MzU2ODc2OHxlYTg1OGRmNC04NA
After: https://screencast.googleplex.com/cast/NTY0NjQzNzI5MDM0NDQ0OHw1MzEyNGIzNS01OA

the resize icon. However, Android resolves the pointer icon from the
view under the pointer, so once a drag moves the pointer off the handle,
the cursor falls back to the mouse cursor icon.

This CL sets the resize icon on the anchor container parent for the
duration of the drag. It covers the web contents, toolbar, etc.

Before: http://screencast/cast/NDg4NjU1NjY3NzUwNTAyNHw3NTIzNmJjOS1jMw
After: http://screencast/cast/NTIwOTQ2ODk2MTgxNjU3NnxhN2UzNGU4Yi01Mw

Avoid crash on reentrant focus changes in FocusManager

Prevent a crash in FocusManager by checking if we are already observing
the focused view before starting a new observation.

During certain reentrant callsites, the focused view may already be
observed, which previously triggered a failing CHECK constraint. This
change replaces the strict CHECK with a conditional check to ensure we
only register the observation if it is not currently active, matching
the intended behavior for addressing reentrant focus changes.

[ReadAloud] Count chunk offsets over trimmed text

TextChunk::start_code_unit_offset now counts over the trimmed chunks
with exactly one separator after each chunk, instead of positions in the
raw segment text. This is the coordinate space highlighter.js builds
from the paragraph texts, so word offsets derived from it (synthesis
response parser, PlaybackTimeline) can be painted directly.

ChunkText() no longer takes a base_offset: chunks always start at 0, and
PrefetchManager shifts each segment's chunks to continue the document's
offsets.

WebUI: Remove redundant ESLint check 'incorrectDollarSignNotation'

This check from @webui-eslint/lit-element-structure is redundant with
the similar rule in @webui-eslint/lit-element-invalid-interface.

The two rules slightly differed in their implementation, where the
former was matching on `this.$['foo-bar']` references whereas the latter
directly inspects the '$: {...}' property definition, but semantically
they are both catching the same issues, so only one is needed.

[Omnibox] Replace View and RecyclerView mocks in LocationBarMediatorUnitTest

Mocking android.view.View and RecyclerView subclasses (such as
OmniboxSuggestionsDropdown) with @Mock generates large ByteBuddy proxy
classes in each Robolectric SDK SandboxClassLoader, contributing to 30s
per-test timeouts on the first test in the class.

Replace @Mock OmniboxSuggestionsDropdown mDropdown and @Mock View fields
(mMicButton, mNavigateButton, mPlusButton, mPlaceholder) with real View
and OmniboxSuggestionsDropdown instances created in setUp().

R=peterkang@google.com

Make the component updater honor --disable-component-update

Under --disable-component-update, only RegisterComponentsForUpdate() was
skipped. Components registered elsewhere, such as the on-device model
manifest, still sent on-demand update checks at startup and started the
update timer, which sent another check about a minute later.

Pass the switch to ComponentUpdateServiceFactory(). With update checks
disabled, CrxUpdateService still registers components, so installed
versions keep working, but it doesn't schedule periodic update checks
and fails on-demand updates without a network request. Update checks for
Chrome for Testing required components are not affected, as those
components are requested explicitly.

ComponentUpdaterPolicyTest makes update checks against a mock server, so
it now removes the switch like other browser tests that do.

NO_IFTTT=enums.xml is updated; its LINT.IfChange(UpdateClientError) block is added in this CL
